note: Let T=(v_0,e_1,v_1,...,e_m,v_m) be a trail with the maximum possible number of edges. Finiteness gives existence and at least one edge gives m>=1. If v_0!=v_m, in the used-edge subgraph H the endpoint v_m has odd degree: the number A of arrivals at v_m is one more than the number D of departures, so deg_H(v_m)=A+D=2D+1. Since deg_G(v_m) is even, some incident edge is not in T, extending T and contradicting maximal length. Thus T is closed. If an edge is omitted, connectedness implies an omitted edge f has an endpoint on V(T): otherwise V(T) has no edge to its nonempty complement and no omitted edge internal to V(T), contradicting connectedness. Rotate the closed trail to start at that endpoint and append f, again contradicting maximal length. Therefore T uses all edges exactly once.
